# An effect's handlers do not run inside the loop that placed the bracket.
# passEffect lifts them to functions on the owner and calls them from the
# settle, which reconciles the whole iteration at once -- so the loop variable
# is out of scope by then, and a handler reading it would compile to a name
# nothing declares.
#
# `on` is the way across, and the handler's parameter is how it arrives.
# Refused up front rather than lowered, because what a user would otherwise
# see is a Go or JS compile error about a generated identifier.

! sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=ht reads_loop_var.sngl
stderr 'reads the loop variable "it"'
stderr 'reads_loop_var.sngl:10:'

# The same bracket, written the way it is meant to be, lowers on every target
# that lowers effects for itself.
sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=ok_ht through_on.sngl
sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=ok_bt through_on.sngl
sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=ok_fy through_on.sngl

# android maps an effect to DisposableEffect, so the pass does not run and the
# question does not arise -- the loop variable is in scope there.
sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=ok_an reads_loop_var.sngl

-- reads_loop_var.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main {
    var (
        items list<string> = ["a", "b"]
        log list<string> = []
    )

    for var it = items {
        effect(on=it, @mount { log.push(it) })
    }

    text(value=log.join(","))
}
-- through_on.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component main {
    var (
        items list<string> = ["a", "b"]
        log list<string> = []
    )

    for var it = items {
        effect(on=it, @mount(v) { log.push(v) })
    }

    text(value=log.join(","))
}
